definitions.gloss: to light; to turn on (a light); to illuminate
definitions.explanation: To switch on or ignite a light source. Used for both modern electric lights and traditional lighting.

examples.japanese: {街灯|がいとう}が{点灯|てんとう}した。
クリスマスツリーのイルミネーションが{点灯|てんとう}された。
examples.english: The Christmas tree illumination was lit.

examples.japanese: {夕方|ゆうがた}になると{自動的|じどうてき}にセンサーが{反応|はんのう}して、{庭|にわ}のライトが{点灯|てんとう}する{仕組|しく}みになっている。
examples.english: In the evening, the sensor activates automatically and the garden lights turn on.

notes:
A somewhat formal word for turning on lights. In everyday speech, {電気|でんき}をつける (to turn on the light) is more common. {点灯|てんとう}する is preferred in technical, official, and ceremonial contexts such as illumination events.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {点灯|てんとう}{式|しき}: lighting ceremony
- {点灯|てんとう}{時間|じかん}: lighting time
- {点灯|てんとう}{確認|かくにん}: light check
- ランプが{点灯|てんとう}する: a lamp lights up
- {警告灯|けいこくとう}が{点灯|てんとう}する: a warning light comes on

SIMILAR WORDS:
- つける: to turn on — everyday word for lights and appliances
- {点|つ}く: to come on (intransitive) — the light turns on by itself
- {消灯|しょうとう}する: to turn off lights — the antonym
